Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — model fit / evals / regression concern

Hi John / Nicole,

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to learn more about Acme's use case for customer support triage and summary. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Summary of needs
- High-precision classification for routing (intent + urgency)
- Concise, extractive summaries for agent handoff (<= 2 sentences)
- Strong safety/PII masking; company policy requires no customer data leaving their VPC for PII fields

Recommended initial model candidates (based on our earlier benchmarks):
- redwood/opt-3b-quant-v2 — best latency/price balance; good extractive summary quality in our internal evals
- meta/llama-2-13b-hf-fp16 — stronger reasoning / edge cases but higher infra cost
- redwood/opt-7b-q4 — middle-ground for higher quality than 3b with better cost than 13b

Attached I’ve included: acme_prompt_set_v1.txt (starter prompt set + example inputs) and model_eval_results.csv (lightbench we ran against the short sample you shared). Also linking the benchmark report and the prompt guide for internal evals: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1A2b3C_example_drive_link

Next steps
1) Please confirm if we can run a limited eval on a sanitized sample (10-50 conversations). We can provide a secure upload guide for VPC/private deploy.
2) Rishi will scope a short eval plan and share a recommended pinning/rollout strategy (to avoid regressions when models update).
3) Schedule a 30m follow-up next week to review the eval results and pricing options — suggested slots Wed/Thu morning PT.

Let me know if that looks right or if you want us to prioritize latency (routing) vs summary quality.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: John Smith <john.smith@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 12:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — model fit / evals / regression concern

Hi John — thanks for surfacing this and for the example. Short answer: yes, we support both pinning and rollbacks, and we have a couple of operational patterns to prevent regressions. Details below.

What likely happened
- We’re rolling out minor model variants (quantization/kernel updates) across pools; in a small number of traces we’ve seen length truncation or tokenization drift affecting extractive summaries. Given your example it sounds consistent with a truncation edge case.

What we can do for Acme
1) Pinning: we can pin your route to a specific model version (e.g., redwood/opt-3b-quant-v2@20260118) so you get deterministic outputs until you opt into an upgrade. Pinning is configurable per-route and supported on Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.
2) Canary + automatic rollback: for non-pinned routes we run canaries and automated quality gates (your eval metrics vs baseline). If a regression is detected on canaries we automatically stop the rollout and can promote the prior variant. We’ll provide logs/commit diffs for any rollout so you can inspect the changes.
3) Fallback routing: we can configure request-level fallback to a higher-quality variant (e.g., opt-7b-q4) for edge-case requests detected by a lightweight classifier. This is slightly higher cost but reduces impact.

Next immediate steps I recommend
- For the eval: we’ll pin to the stable tag redwood/opt-3b-quant-v2@20260118 by default. If the small sample you’ll share looks good we can plan a controlled canary to the latest variant with your approval.
- I’ve attached the quick regression diff we ran comparing 20260118 -> 20260205 on our internal prompt set (regression_diff_20260211.png) and the eval csv we used. These show the precision/recall delta on action-item extraction.

Operational notes
- We store model tags and rollout IDs in the console and provide an endpoint to query the active model for a route (useful for audits).
- For Private customers we provide a config file to pin at deploy-time.

Happy to jump on a 30m runbook session with your SREs to walk through the rollback steps and show how to interpret the diffs.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
